overall_summary: Deduplication and recency weighting of the FACTVERSE dataset reveal clear performance stratification across niches. Space and extreme planetary scenarios dominate the top-performing tier, particularly when framed through hypothetical curiosity ('What If You Fell Into...') or extreme planetary phenomena. Specifically, videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes), and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) significantly outperform older standard historical or biological facts. Engagement metrics (likes-per-view) are highest on extreme astronomical 'what-if' hooks and bizarre physical anomalies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on hypothetical falls into exotic worlds ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') generate high views and strong like-to-view ratios (>3.7% like rate).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on surreal astronomical scenarios, specifically targeting extreme physical environments and hypothetical human interaction with bizarre celestial bodies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring extreme planetary anomalies ('The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b', 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') consistently drive high views (700-1000+ views) compared to generic space facts.
winning_patterns.action: Structure hooks around counterintuitive, visually striking planetary conditions (e.g., extreme weather, bizarre compositions, or impossible physics in space).

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics centered around psychological facts ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head') show very low view velocity (often under 60-70 views) and poor engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard human psychology and memory hacks unless tied to a high-concept sci-fi or dark mystery angle.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorter animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' published multiple times without a strong narrative hook show stagnant or declining performance over repeated tracking cycles.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid simple textbook animal stats; if covering animals, pivot to cinematic animal survival or extreme prehistoric/evolutionary paradoxes.
